dedupe_keys.name: nasa fmdtools version 2 python toolkit for simulating hazard propagation and quantifying resilience of complex engineered systems

description: fmdtools is a NASA Ames Python toolkit for simulating the dynamic effects of hazardous scenarios in complex engineered systems and analysing their resilience, released as open source through the NASA Software Catalog (case ARC-18750-1A, version 2.0 of December 2023). Contents: three components: model definition constructs for concise early specification of a system's high-level structure and behaviours; simulation methods that quantify system performance and the propagation of hazards over a wide range of operational scenarios and model types; and analysis methods that quantify resilience and summarise and visualise behaviours. Version 2.0 adds constructs for human operators, environmental dynamics, systems-of-systems interactions, communications and distributed situation awareness, hazard simulation at function or component level and at system level, and search of parameters and states that increase resilience or drive the system to failure. Producer: NASA Ames. Coverage: generic. Format and access: open source Python package for Windows, Linux and macOS, linked from the catalogue. Licence: NASA open source release. Caveats: models are functional abstractions written by the user, so results depend on assumed behaviours and fault rates. Simulation uses: modelling failure propagation and recovery in engineered and infrastructure systems, comparing the resilience of design alternatives, and cascading fault scenarios. Related records: NASA Zappy (model-nasa-zappy-load-flow-power-system-design-openmdao) is another NASA open design tool.
